subject: Creativity
title: Adolescent Imagination: The Identity Laboratory
description: A quick win: understand Adolescent Imagination: The Identity Laboratory.

hook.text: Teenagers imagine possible selves — rock star, activist, CEO — cycling through identities like trying on clothes.

buildup.text: Erik Erikson called adolescence an identity moratorium — a phase of trying possible adult selves.

discovery.text: The prefrontal cortex is still developing until age 25. This 'incompleteness' enables wilder, more expansive imagining.

twist.text: Social media gives teenage imagination an audience, amplifying both expression and social anxiety.

climax.text: Teens with rich 'possible selves' imagery are more resilient — they can imagine recovery from setbacks.

punchline.text: Teenagers aren't confused. They're auditioning for their future selves.

quiz.question: What did Erik Erikson call the adolescent period of identity experimentation?
